items.name: Swiss / International Typographic
items.vibe: Silence with a grid running through it — everything decorative has been removed, and what survived feels inevitable.
signature: 12-column grid with a hard baseline — every line-height a multiple of 4px
Hierarchy from the type scale alone: size and weight, never color
One accent color covering under 5% of the surface (classically red)
Hairlines instead of shadows: 1px solid rules, border-radius 0-4px
Content column capped near 65ch with margins that feel almost wasteful
doNotUseFor: products that need to feel warm or fun — this style reads as cold by construction
dense dashboards, where the whitespace budget this needs does not exist
brands whose only real asset is personality — this hides it
teams without a strict reviewer: one 13px margin breaks the whole illusion
checklist: Every spacing value comes from the scale — no arbitrary numbers, ever
If you reach for a shadow you have left the style; use a hairline or more space
The grid must survive 320px — collapse to one column but keep the baseline
Cheap to build, unforgiving to get right: budget review time, not dev time

items.name: Glassmorphism
items.vibe: Frosted panes floating over something colorful — light, layered, and faintly expensive.
signature: backdrop-filter: blur(12px) saturate(160%) over an rgba(255,255,255,0.10) surface
1px hairline border at ~20% white plus an inset top highlight to fake the glass edge
A saturated or photographic layer underneath — glass over flat gray is just gray
Layered z-planes, each pane with its own blur radius to imply thickness
Wide soft shadow (0 8px 32px rgba(0,0,0,.2)) to lift the pane off the backdrop
doNotUseFor: data-dense tables — blur destroys the row-scanning edge you depend on
long-form reading — live background under paragraphs is exhausting
anything that must certify WCAG AA on text: the backdrop is never a known color
low-end mobile and Android webviews — every pane is an offscreen render pass
print and export views, where the whole effect flattens to gray mush
checklist: Keep body text off the blurred layer — put it on a solid or near-solid chip
Test on a busy photo AND a plain background; if it vanishes on plain, the style is doing nothing
Ship a @supports not (backdrop-filter: blur(1px)) fallback with an opaque surface
Cap it at 3-5 blurred surfaces per view — each one costs a separate render pass
Honor prefers-reduced-transparency

items.name: Neumorphism (Soft UI)
items.vibe: Controls extruded from one sheet of soft plastic — beautiful in a screenshot, ambiguous the moment you try to use it.
signature: Two shadows per element: light -6px -6px 12px #ffffff and dark 6px 6px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.15)
Element and background share the exact same fill — the shape exists only as shadow
Pressed state flips the same shadows to inset
Large radii (16-24px) so the extrusion reads as soft rather than machined
A single desaturated base hue (around #e0e5ec) across the entire surface
doNotUseFor: forms — inputs and buttons have no reliable affordance and no honest focus state
anything accessibility-critical: low contrast IS the aesthetic, you cannot fix it and keep it
government, healthcare, finance, or any regulated interface
low-vision or older audiences — the edges simply are not there
dark mode — the light-source trick collapses without a bright base
dense layouts — every control needs 12px+ of clear shadow room
checklist: Add a real border and a contrast-bearing focus ring — accept that it breaks the look, ship it anyway
Never encode state in shadow alone; change color or label too
Run the 3:1 UI-component check on every control edge — most will fail
If 'is this a button?' takes longer than a second to answer, pick another style

items.name: Brutalism (Web Brutalism)
items.vibe: The raw document showing through on purpose — default links, system type, and zero apology.
signature: Barely-styled defaults: system or Times body, blue underlined links, visible borders
border: 2px solid #000 with border-radius: 0 — no shadows, no gradients, no easing
Pure #000 on #fff with one screaming accent, usually #ff0000 or #0000ff
Layout that exposes document flow — left-aligned, ragged, no centering ceremony
Type at extremes: 12px body sitting next to a 120px headline
doNotUseFor: enterprise and b2b buyers — it reads as unfinished, not intentional
e-commerce checkout, where friction reads as broken and kills conversion
audiences who never opted into the joke
products asking to be trusted with money or health data
checklist: Keep the default focus outline — removing it is the one move that would make this style fail
Raw is a choice, not an excuse: tap targets are still 44px
Intentionally ugly must still pass 4.5:1 — that yellow on white does not
Semantic HTML is doing the accessibility work here; do not replace it with divs

items.name: Neo-Brutalism
items.vibe: Brutalism after a sugar rush — thick black outlines, hard offset shadows, and candy color that shouts.
signature: border: 3px solid #000 on every surface, border-radius 0-8px
Hard offset shadow with zero blur: box-shadow: 6px 6px 0 #000
Press translates the element into its own shadow: translate(4px,4px) and shrink the offset
Flat saturated fills — yellow, pink, lime, cyan — always with black ink on top
Geometric sans at 700-900 weight, tight tracking
doNotUseFor: finance, legal, or healthcare — the toy vocabulary quietly undercuts trust
data-dense screens: 3px borders eat the pixel budget and every row shouts equally
long reading, where saturated fills fatigue within a paragraph
brands that must feel premium — this reads cheap by design
checklist: Every interactive element needs the press-translate — without it the shadow is just decoration
Check black text on your brightest fill: lime and yellow pass, mid-blue does not
In dark mode swap outlines to white or the entire system disappears
Three fills maximum, or it stops being bold and starts being noise

items.name: Flat / Modern Flat
items.vibe: Clean shapes and clear color with nothing pretending to be a physical object — the safe default of the modern web.
signature: Solid fills, border-radius 6-12px, one subtle elevation tier
Neutral gray ramp plus one primary and one destructive — shadcn token shape
Elevation from a 1px border and 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.05), never a gradient
4/8px spacing scale; type scale 12/14/16/20/24/30/36
Hover is a 4-8% tint shift, not a transform
doNotUseFor: brands that need to be remembered — this is the style everyone already shipped
launches and campaigns that must stop the scroll
luxury or fashion, where it reads as an unfinished template
checklist: Pick one elevation system — border OR shadow — and never mix them on the same tier
If it looks like the default template, add exactly one signature move: type, radius, or accent
Do not ship gray-400 on white; that is the classic flat contrast failure

items.name: Material Design (M3 / Expressive)
items.vibe: Digital paper with rules — surfaces at defined elevations and ink that ripples where you touch it.
signature: Tonal elevation — surfaces tint toward the primary hue as they rise, not just cast shadow
Ripple from the touch point; state layers at 8/12/16% opacity
Roles rather than colors: primary / on-primary / surface / on-surface tokens
4dp grid, 48dp minimum target, FAB anchored bottom-right
Corner radius as a token scale (4/8/16/28dp), full-round for pills
bestFor: teams that need a complete spec off the shelf
doNotUseFor: ios-first products, where it reads as a bad port
brands with their own strong visual language — M3 overwrites it
marketing sites: this is an application system, not an editorial one
teams who will only adopt half of it — partial Material reads as broken Material
checklist: Use the token roles; hardcoding hex defeats the entire tonal system
No ripples and no tonal elevation means you are not doing Material — use flat instead
Audit dynamic color output: user wallpapers generate pairs you never tested

items.name: Skeuomorphism
items.vibe: Software pretending to be a real object — stitched leather, brushed metal, and a bevel you could almost feel.
signature: Multi-stop gradients on every control to fake a light source from above
Inner bevel: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.6) highlight over a dark bottom inset
Repeating raster texture on surfaces — linen, felt, brushed aluminum
Drop shadow plus a faint reflection to seat the object in its scene
Letterpress type via text-shadow: 0 1px 0 #fff
doNotUseFor: productivity apps — the chrome eats the budget the content needed
products that must scale to many screens: every control is bespoke art
responsive layouts, because textures and bevels do not reflow
modern brand work, where it reads as 2011 unless the nostalgia is the point
checklist: Every texture ships as an optimized tile or you have just added megabytes
Keep text on a flat region and check contrast against the darkest pixel, not the average
Pick one light direction — top — and honor it on every single element
Affordance is this style's superpower; do not waste it by making everything look pressable

items.name: Claymorphism
items.vibe: Soft 3D blobs that look squeezable — puffy, rounded, and relentlessly friendly.
signature: Huge radii — border-radius: 32-50px on everything, containers included
Double inner shadow to inflate: inset -8px -8px 16px rgba(255,255,255,.5), inset 8px 8px 16px rgba(0,0,0,.08)
One wide outer shadow tinted with the element hue, never black: 0 20px 40px rgba(120,90,255,.25)
Pastel fills on a light room — clay never sits on black
Rounded geometric sans with generous letter spacing
doNotUseFor: enterprise or professional tools — nothing serious survives a 48px radius
data-dense views, where the padding the shape demands wastes half the screen
dark mode — clay needs a light room to read as clay at all
text-heavy pages
checklist: Pastel fills fail 4.5:1 with white labels — use a dark ink instead
Keep radius proportional; 48px on a 56px button silently becomes a pill
Tint shadows with the element hue — black shadows turn clay into plastic

items.name: Bento Grid
items.vibe: A lunchbox of unequal cards, each compartment sized to its content, the whole thing snapping into a satisfying whole.
signature: display: grid with explicit grid-template-areas — deliberate unequal spans, not auto-fill
One uniform gap (16-24px) and one uniform radius across every tile — the only constants
Each tile owns exactly one idea: a stat, a visual, a quote, a live demo
A hero tile at 2x2 anchoring the composition
Tile-level backgrounds mixed on purpose: some solid, some gradient, some full-bleed
doNotUseFor: sequential content — a grid promises you can read in any order
long lists of like items: that is a table or a list, and bento adds nothing
mobile-first products, where it collapses to a boring stack under 768px
content that grows unpredictably — the composition is hand-tuned and breaks on the 9th tile
checklist: DOM order must match reading order — never use grid placement to reorder meaning
Design the one-column collapse deliberately; the default stack loses all hierarchy
If every tile is the same size you built a card grid and called it bento
Whole-tile click targets need a real anchor element, not onClick on a div

items.name: Editorial / Magazine
items.vibe: Print art direction on a screen — a huge serif headline, a real column, and photography allowed to breathe.
signature: Display serif at 48-120px against 16-19px body — extreme scale contrast
Measure locked to 60-75ch; multi-column only above 1024px
Drop cap via ::first-letter { float: left; font-size: 4em; line-height: .8 }
Asymmetric grid — text column offset, images breaking into the margin
Pull quotes and captions in a contrasting family or italic at small size
doNotUseFor: applications — there is no ui vocabulary here, only content
dashboards and forms
content that is actually short: an editorial shell around 200 words looks abandoned
sites with no photography budget — this style is half imagery by weight
checklist: Body at 18px+ with 1.6 line-height — this style lives or dies on reading comfort
Subset the display face; 200KB of serif for one headline is a bad trade
Never multi-column below 1024px — a 30ch column is unreadable
Captions are content, not decoration; style them, do not forget them

items.name: Terminal / CLI
items.vibe: A monospace prompt on a dark screen — as if the product is talking to you in its own language.
signature: One monospace family everywhere — JetBrains Mono, Berkeley Mono, or ui-monospace
A character grid: sizing in ch units rather than px
Blinking block cursor from @keyframes on a ::after element
Box-drawing borders drawn with characters instead of CSS borders
Dark base (#0a0a0a-#111) with one phosphor accent and syntax-color hierarchy
doNotUseFor: non-technical audiences — it reads as an error screen, not a product
long prose: monospace measurably slows reading speed
mobile, because a character grid does not reflow
buyer-facing pages, as opposed to user-facing ones
checklist: ASCII art and box-drawing need aria-hidden — to a screen reader it is pure noise
Give anything drawn with characters a real text alternative
Classic #00ff00 on black is 15:1 and still exhausting; use a desaturated green
Do not set prose in mono past a single paragraph

items.name: Retro / Y2K
items.vibe: The year 2000 imagined the future as chrome bubbles and lens flare, and this is that future, played straight.
signature: Chrome gradients with a hard specular band across the middle
Bubble buttons: pill shape, inset white highlight, colored gloss beneath
Iridescent fills via conic-gradient with rainbow stops
Starburst, sparkle and lens-flare accents as SVG overlays
Chunky rounded sans with a chrome text-shadow outline
doNotUseFor: b2b anything
products with a long shelf life — this trend dates faster than you can rebrand
content-heavy sites, where the ornament fights every word
accessibility-regulated contexts
checklist: Never set body copy in chrome — reserve gradient text for exactly one headline
Every sparkle and flare is decorative: aria-hidden plus empty alt
Keep a boring, legible fallback for checkout and form pages
Gradient text via background-clip needs a solid fallback in forced-colors mode

items.name: Vaporwave
items.vibe: A dead mall at 3am rendered in pink and cyan — nostalgia, irony, and a sunset grid stretching to nowhere.
signature: Magenta-to-cyan gradient sky over a perspective grid floor: rotateX(75deg) on a repeating-linear-gradient
Chromatic aberration — duplicate the text offset 2px in cyan and magenta
Scanline overlay: repeating-linear-gradient(rgba(0,0,0,.15) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px)
Headline bloom via text-shadow: 0 0 12px currentColor
Statue, palm and katakana imagery used as texture rather than content
doNotUseFor: anything commercial that needs to be taken seriously
products with real utility screens behind the marketing
audiences outside the in-joke — this is a subculture reference, not a look
photosensitivity-safe requirements: glitch plus scanlines is a trigger stack
checklist: Scanlines and glitch must respect prefers-reduced-motion and be switchable off
Cyan on magenta is roughly 1.5:1 — real text goes on a solid dark plate
Nothing flashes faster than 3Hz; that is a seizure threshold, not a style note
Chromatic aberration on body text is illegible — headline only

items.name: Cyberpunk / Neon
items.vibe: A rain-slick night city in a browser — black surfaces, electric edges, information that glows at you.
signature: Near-black base (#05060a) with 1px neon edges: border 1px solid #0ff plus box-shadow 0 0 8px #0ff
HUD panel shapes cut with clip-path: polygon() for angled corners
Two-accent tension — cyan and magenta, or amber and teal, never a single hue
Glitch keyframes on hover: clip-path steps plus small translate
Wide-tracked uppercase mono or tech sans for every label
doNotUseFor: long reading — glow blurs the glyph edges your eye tracks
professional b2b tools
light mode: this style has no light variant worth shipping
large data tables, where every glowing edge competes for the same attention
checklist: Glow is decoration — the underlying contrast must pass with the glow removed
Saturated blue text on black is the worst case for astigmatism; use cyan or amber
Gate every glitch animation behind prefers-reduced-motion
Two accents. A third turns cyberpunk into a christmas tree

items.name: Dark Luxury
items.vibe: Black, gold, and a great deal of empty space — the confidence of something that never mentions its price.
signature: Near-black base (#0b0b0c) — pure #000 kills the depth
Metallic accent as a gradient, not a flat color: linear-gradient(135deg,#bfa06a,#f0dfa8,#8c6f3f) with background-clip: text
Whitespace at twice the normal scale — sections at 160px+ vertical padding
A high-contrast display serif, or a light wide-tracked sans in uppercase
Hairline dividers at 8-12% white and no shadows anywhere
doNotUseFor: value or discount brands — the vocabulary flatly contradicts the offer
dense product catalogs: gold hairlines do not scale to 200 skus
light mode, where the luxury signal literally was the darkness
text-heavy or utility screens
checklist: Gold (#bfa06a) on black is about 5:1 — fine for headings, verify it at 14px
No 200-weight type below 18px on black; thin strokes bloom on dark screens
background-clip: text needs a solid-color fallback for forced-colors mode
If you are adding a shadow, the style has already failed

items.name: Organic / Earthy
items.vibe: Warm clay, paper and leaf tones in shapes that never met a right angle — calm and vaguely handmade.
signature: Warm off-white base (#faf7f2) — every neutral carries a hue, never #fff
Terracotta, sage, ochre and clay at low saturation
Blob shapes: border-radius: 60% 40% 55% 45% / 45% 55% 40% 60%
Paper grain texture overlaid at 3-6% opacity
Humanist serif or rounded sans at a generous 1.7 line-height
doNotUseFor: technical and developer products, where it reads as unserious
urgency-driven ui — alerts, trading, ops: this palette cannot signal danger
dense data, because muted tones give you no contrast steps to work with
brands that need to feel precise or clinical
checklist: Push ink to around #2c2822 — warm mid-tones on warm backgrounds fail 4.5:1 fast
Reserve one saturated color for errors; a muted-only palette cannot warn anyone
Grain overlays need pointer-events: none and aria-hidden
Blob shapes must not clip text at narrow widths — test at 320px

items.name: Hand-Drawn / Sketch
items.vibe: As if someone sketched the interface on a napkin and it happened to work — wobbly, human, disarming.
signature: Rough.js, or an SVG filter chaining feTurbulence and feDisplacementMap to fray every stroke
Hand-lettered display face (Caveat, Patrick Hand, Excalifont) paired with a clean sans for body
Cross-hatch SVG pattern fills instead of solid color
A small random rotation per element — transform: rotate(-0.6deg) — so nothing is exactly square
Paper background: off-white with faint ruled or grid lines
doNotUseFor: anything conveying precision — sketch says 'draft', which is fatal next to a price or a dose
enterprise buyers
dense ui, because frayed borders need slack around them to read
brands where the wobble will be reported as a rendering bug
checklist: Never set body copy in the hand-drawn face — display only, always
SVG displacement filters repaint on every resize; rasterize anything static
Ask once: could a user think this is broken? If maybe, halve the wobble
Hand-lettered faces are hard for dyslexic readers — keep the clean sans doing the work

items.name: Memphis / Playful
items.vibe: 80s design-school chaos — squiggles, confetti shapes and clashing color, arranged just carefully enough to work.
signature: Loose decorative SVG shapes — squiggle, zigzag, half-circle, terrazzo dots — scattered behind content
A clashing-on-purpose palette: 4-6 saturated hues with no neutral hierarchy
Terrazzo and dot patterns as full section backgrounds
Elements rotated 3-10deg and deliberately overlapping the grid
Fat geometric sans with tight tracking
doNotUseFor: any application ui — there is no consistent hierarchy left to build on
b2b and finance
content-heavy pages, where decoration competes with every paragraph
products needing a calm focused state: writing, meditation, ops consoles
checklist: Text never sits directly on a pattern — give it a solid plate
Nominate one hue as the real primary or nothing will look clickable
Decorative shapes get aria-hidden and pointer-events: none
Rotation must not push targets under 44px or off-canvas on mobile

items.name: Gradient Mesh
items.vibe: Soft clouds of color bleeding into one another — a background that feels alive without ever asking for attention.
signature: Stacked radial-gradient() layers at different positions on one element — the cheap, correct mesh
Or 3-5 absolutely-positioned blobs at filter: blur(80px) with mix-blend-mode: screen
OKLCH color stops so the blend never passes through gray
Contained by overflow: hidden, with content on a solid plate above it
Slow drift: keyframes translating blobs 5-10% over 20s or more
doNotUseFor: behind body text — a moving color field under paragraphs is unreadable
as the full-page background of an application
behind data visualization: it corrupts every color you plot on top
low-end mobile if blur-based — blur(80px) is a full-viewport pass every frame
checklist: Prefer layered radial-gradient() over blurred divs — same look, a fraction of the cost
Text on the mesh needs a scrim or a solid card; there is no fixed contrast value here
Animate transform only — animating gradient stops repaints the entire layer
Interpolate in OKLCH; sRGB blends go muddy through the middle

items.name: Monochrome
items.vibe: One hue, many values — the discipline of a black-and-white photograph applied to an interface.
signature: One hue across ten lightness steps — hierarchy from value, never from color
The accent is a value jump (white on black), not a second hue
Weight and size carry emphasis: font-weight 600 replaces a colored label
Images desaturated with filter: grayscale(1), restoring color on hover
Hairline borders in the same hue at 10-15% alpha
bestFor: apps where content supplies the color
doNotUseFor: status-heavy ui — you have given up the channel that says success, warning, error
data visualization beyond about four series
e-commerce where product color is the thing being sold
onboarding for non-expert users: color is a wayfinding tool you are discarding
checklist: Reserve exactly one color for destructive and error states — a monochrome error is negligent
Test the value steps in grayscale at 200% zoom; if two steps merge, delete one
Do not let 'monochrome' quietly mean 'low contrast' — use the full 0-100 range
This is the one style that is inherently colorblind-safe; do not throw that away for an accent

items.name: High-Contrast / Accessible-First
items.vibe: Built so nobody has to squint — big type, hard edges, and every state announcing exactly what it is.
signature: Body at 18px+, 4.5:1 minimum everywhere, 7:1 on headings where it is affordable
A focus ring nobody can miss: outline: 3px solid with outline-offset: 2px — never outline: none
Every state doubled — color plus icon plus text, never color alone
44x44 minimum targets with real space between them
prefers-contrast: more and forced-colors paths actually implemented, not stubbed
bestFor: anything under WCAG, ADA or EAA obligation
doNotUseFor: brands competing on aesthetic distinction — this style spends its budget elsewhere on purpose
expert-facing dense tools, where 18px type costs rows the daily user actually wants
fashion-forward marketing
as an alibi: it is the floor for every other style here, not a box to tick once
checklist: This is a floor, not a ceiling — every other style in this database still owes WCAG AA
Verify with a real screen reader, not a lighthouse score
Never ship accessibility as a toggle; that is two products, one of them neglected
Contrast alone is not accessibility — check focus order, labels, and error recovery

items.name: Corporate Clean
items.vibe: Blue, trustworthy and utterly unsurprising — the visual language of a company that wants procurement to say yes.
signature: A blue primary near #2563eb, neutral grays, one supporting accent
Card sections with 1px borders and border-radius: 8px
The known page order: hero, logo wall, 3-up features, testimonial, pricing, CTA
Neutral grotesk (Inter, Söhne) at 400 and 600 — no display weights
Single stroke-weight icons; flat abstract illustration
doNotUseFor: consumer products competing on delight
brands whose wedge is being different — this actively erases differentiation
agency and creative work, where clients will assume you have no taste
developer audiences, who read this as marketing rather than substance
checklist: The trust signals do the work — logos, numbers, testimonials. Without them this is a blue template
Check your link blue on white: #2563eb passes 4.5:1, most lighter blues do not
One accent besides the blue, maximum
If the hero could carry any competitor's logo unchanged, the brand is missing

items.name: Data-Dense / Dashboard
items.vibe: Bloomberg energy — maximum information per pixel, tuned for someone who stares at it for eight hours.
signature: Row height 28-32px, font-size 13px, line-height 1.3 — deliberately tight
font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums with every number right-aligned
Zebra striping or hairline separators at 6-8% — never full borders
Sticky header and sticky first column; virtualized rows past ~100
Color reserved for meaning — up, down, alert — and never for decoration
doNotUseFor: marketing pages — density reads as intimidating to a first-time visitor
mobile-first products: this pattern assumes 1440px and a mouse
occasional users — density is a trade you make only for daily experts
layering with glass, neumorphism, gradients or texture: that combination is a bug, not a style
checklist: Tabular numerals or your columns will never align — this one is non-negotiable
Ship a density toggle (comfortable / compact); do not force 13px on everyone
Full keyboard navigation, or power users will resent it by week two
Virtualize past 100 rows: the CSS is cheap, the DOM is not
13px type and tight targets are a real accessibility debt — pay it with the toggle and zoom support

items.name: Motion-Driven
items.vibe: The page performs as you scroll — things assemble, parallax and reveal, and the story lives in the movement.
signature: Scroll-linked timelines via animation-timeline: view() or GSAP ScrollTrigger
Staggered reveals — 40-80ms per child, translateY(16px) plus opacity
Only transform and opacity animate; anything else drops frames
Easing with character — cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1) — 200-400ms for ui, 600-1200ms for narrative
One pinned section where scroll drives a sequence rather than the page position
doNotUseFor: utility ui — motion between the user and the task is a tax paid on every single visit
content users need to find fast: scroll-reveal hides text from Ctrl+F and from readers
long pages on low-end devices
products people return to daily — the delight decays to annoyance by the third visit
checklist: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce must show the final state instantly — not a faster animation
Never scroll-jack; the user owns the scrollbar
Content exists in the DOM and is findable before its reveal ever runs
Parallax is the classic vestibular trigger — keep it under 10% displacement or drop it
Budget it: if the hero choreography costs 200KB of JS, cut the choreography

items.name: 3D / Spatial
items.vibe: Objects with real depth you can orbit — the screen stops being a page and becomes a stage.
signature: perspective: 1000px on the container plus transform-style: preserve-3d for CSS-only depth
Or a real scene — Three.js / React Three Fiber canvas with constrained orbit controls
Tilt on hover: pointer position mapped to rotateX/rotateY within ±10deg
One key light plus a rim light, and a grounded contact shadow so the object does not float
Progressive load: poster image first, model second, with a hard budget on the glb
doNotUseFor: content sites — a webgl canvas as decoration is a 500KB tax on every visitor
mobile-heavy audiences: thermal throttling and battery drain are real and measurable
anything needing SEO on the 3D content — canvas contents do not exist to a crawler
utility ui, because nobody wants to orbit their settings page
checklist: Every canvas needs a DOM equivalent — the content must exist outside the scene
Ship a poster frame and lazy-load the scene; never block LCP on a model
Cap pixel ratio at 2 and pause the raf loop when the canvas is off-screen
Respect prefers-reduced-motion: no auto-orbit, no camera drift
Canvas is opaque to assistive tech and rarely keyboard-operable — plan for both or drop it

items.name: Typographic / Type-First
items.vibe: The words are the design — scale, weight and spacing do everything an image would have done.
signature: One giant headline: font-size: clamp(3rem, 12vw, 12rem) with line-height .9 and negative tracking
A variable font animated on one axis — weight or width — instead of a second family
Optical tuning: text-wrap: balance on headings, text-wrap: pretty on body
Hierarchy from two sizes and two weights: no color, no rules, no boxes
Type as layout — the text block is the composition, imagery optional
doNotUseFor: localization-heavy sites — German and Finnish will detonate your 12vw headline
cms-driven content, where every headline needs hand-tuning to look right
applications and forms
teams where a marketer edits copy without a designer seeing it
checklist: Never size body text in vw — it ignores the user's font-size setting; clamp() with a rem floor
Test the longest translation you will ever ship, then add 30%
Subset the variable font and set font-display: swap — unsubsetted it can be 300KB
text-wrap: balance on headings is the cheapest quality win available here

items.name: Illustrated
items.vibe: Custom drawings carry the personality — the interface is just a frame around characters made for it.
signature: A defined system — one line weight, one palette, one perspective. Not stock, not mixed sources
SVG spot illustrations at anchor points: hero, empty state, onboarding, error
Illustration palette derived from the ui palette and desaturated ~15% so it recedes
Characters carrying the emotion copy cannot: 404, empty, success
Layout stays plain — illustration is the only ornament in the room
doNotUseFor: teams without an illustrator or budget — mixed stock art is worse than no art
dense professional tools, where a mascot in a trading ui is a distraction
brands needing gravitas: legal, security, enterprise infrastructure
screens users see daily — the joke gets old but the file size does not
checklist: Decide per image: decorative gets an empty alt, informative gets a real description
Every illustration needs a dark-mode variant or a plate it survives on
Run SVGO — a Figma-exported SVG is routinely 5x larger than it needs to be
One illustrator, one system. Two styles on one site reads as a hack

items.name: Photographic / Full-Bleed
items.vibe: A photograph the size of the window with a few words on it — the image is the product and everything else gets out of the way.
signature: height: 100svh image with object-fit: cover and an art-directed picture element per breakpoint
A scrim for legibility: linear-gradient(to top, rgba(0,0,0,.65), transparent 60%) — not a flat overlay
Minimal type on the image: one headline, one line, one CTA
Focal point preserved across crops via object-position per breakpoint
Everything else neutral — the photograph is the only color in the system
doNotUseFor: products without professional photography — a stock hero is worse than a plain gradient
any screen carrying more than ~15 words over the image
data-conscious markets and slow connections: the hero IS your LCP
content that changes often, where every new photo needs the same art direction
checklist: Check the headline against the LIGHTEST pixel behind it, not the average
Scrim, always — the photo you tested is not the photo the CMS will receive
AVIF/WebP, picture-element art direction, fetchpriority high on the hero and lazy on the rest
Set explicit dimensions or aspect-ratio: this style is a CLS machine
Text baked into an image is invisible to search and to screen readers

items.name: Aurora / Glow
items.vibe: Dark surfaces lit from behind by slow-moving colored light — the look that says 'serious tech, tastefully'.
signature: Dark base (#08090c) with one or two blurred radial gradients bleeding in from the top edge
Glowing 1px borders from a linear-gradient border-image or a masked pseudo-element
Spotlight follows cursor: CSS vars --x/--y updated on pointermove driving a radial-gradient
Very slow drift (30-60s) so the light breathes instead of animating
Everything else restrained — neutral type, small radii, hairline dividers
doNotUseFor: light mode — the glow needs darkness to exist at all
non-technical buyers: this is a genre signal, not universal appeal
content-heavy reading, where ambient light under long text is fatiguing
brands that need to look distinct — as of 2026 every dev tool already looks like this
checklist: Body text on the dark base must hit 4.5:1 — the tasteful dim gray is usually 3.8:1
Pointer-driven glow updates a CSS var; never re-render React on pointermove
Layer radial-gradients rather than blur(100px) on a div for the ambient wash
This look is everywhere now — if you need differentiation, this is not it
